Look at this narrow twenty-mile gap of water between Bali and Lombok in Indonesia.
On this side, you have Asian tigers, monkeys, rhinos, and elephants roaming the jungle.
Cross just twenty miles to the other side, and every single Asian mammal completely vanishes.
Instead, you find tree kangaroos, marsupials, and cockatoos native to Australia.
Even birds that could easily fly across refuse to cross this invisible line.
Why? During the Ice Age, sea levels dropped over three hundred feet, connecting Asia to Bali.
Tigers could literally walk across dry land - until they hit this exact gap.
Because right here lies an ancient oceanic trench over one thousand feet deep that never dried up.
It kept Asia and Australia biologically isolated for fifty million years, and the line is still unbroken today.
